newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coca-Cola Philippine unit sets $1.7 bln expansion.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Philippine unit sets $1.7 bln expansion.

text.p: Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc (CCBPI) unveiled on Thursday a spending programme of $1.7 billion over the next five years to strengthen its position in the soft drinks industry in the Philippines.

"Coca-Cola has opened its 21st bottling plant in the Philippines as part of a $1.7 billion five-year spending programme to meet growing product demand and strengthen its leadership position in the country," the company said in a statement.

CCBPI is 70 percent-owned by food and beverage conglomerate San Miguel Corp and 30 percent by the U.S.-based Coca-Cola Company. It is the number one soft drinks company in the country with a total market share of 75 percent.
Coca-Cola Philippines said the new bottling plant will have an initial annual production capacity of over 31 million cases.
The new plant, located in Laguna south of Manila, is one of the largest soft drinks complexes in the world built at a total investment of 3.1 billion pesos ($118 million), the statement said.

"The Philippines has become one of our most important markets internationally," the statement quoted Douglas Ivester, president and chief operating officer of The Coca-Cola Company, as saying during the inauguration of the new plant on Thursday.
Officials said the expansion in the Philippines is a wide ranging programme that would include plants, products, and marketing.
